articles.title: Architecture and Neurodivergence: Designing for Different Ways of Perceiving Space
articles.summary: Wide doorways, properly designed ramps, and elevators are essential to a building's accessibility. But whether people can actually use its spaces also depends on the sensory conditions they offer. For some neurodivergent people, this is critical, as bright lights, overlapping sounds, or confusing circulation routes can prevent them from staying in a space and participating in activities.

articles.title: House in Dahiya / Studio Toggle
articles.summary: House in Dahiya gives nothing to the street. On a quiet road in Dahiyat Abdullah Al Salem, one of central Kuwait City's most premium residential districts, a stepped mass of raw exposed concrete rises between two date palms. Its principal facades are closed, and the entrance sits back behind dark vertical fins. The brief asked for exactly this: a house closed and unreadable from the street, yet open, light and generous within, and able to withstand Kuwait's heat, dust and salt air with little upkeep. Behind the sealed mass lies a protected inner world with its own climate, color and calm.

articles.title: Automatic Drop Down Seals for Doors
articles.summary: The automatic door bottom is a clever bit of engineering that prevents under-door drafts, without installing a skirt that drags across your floor. Also called an automatic drop seal, it consists of an aluminum extrusion mounted in a dado cut into the bottom of the door. A little brass plunger protrudes from one end on the hinge side. As you close the door, the plunger is forced inside the assembly, where it triggers the spring-loaded seal to drop to the threshold, sealing the gap. Opening the door causes the seal to retract.
